notes.title: Speed Limit Anniversary + 60% OFF + Steam Trading Cards!
notes.content:
So! It has been exactly a year since Speed Limit launched on Steam (and other platforms), and we were pretty entertained with watching you guys (who recorded gameplay on YouTube and other streaming platforms) die in various situations in Speed Limit.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/MqACPGz.gif[/img]

Of course, we didn't forget about you guys who like to take it easy, so we created a mode where you can roam around in great-looking Neon scenery while listening to an awesome synthwave soundtrack. Along with a completely free Arcade Mode. And in our final update of 2021, we also added a Kiosk mode which allows you to set up and play the game on your own coin-operated arcade machines!

[previewyoutube=7_OL0borVkM;full][/previewyoutube]

So, thank you. THANK YOU ALL for playing Speed Limit and sticking with us.

In this past year, the cross-platform sales of Speed Limit have surpassed all previous titles from our small studio, and even on Steam we are close to hitting the 100 reviews mark, a milestone we are sure to reach with this anniversary update!

We are glad to still have the Very Positive review aggregate, as well as all the awards and nominations we received in the past year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/1075d6e1668f5ed3b0424616e5a6cbbcb57f1686.jpg[/img]

For all of you who enjoyed this game, be sure to check out our upcoming pixel-art action title: Midwintär.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1724900/Midwintar/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/bbe671dd76d811e5b682ab510d8cb3577ef8ac3d.png[/img][/url]

Btw, here's a cool gameplay preview, too!

[previewyoutube=eknUvN9wiw0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]BUT! We are here because of something else.[/h2]

Speed Limit is getting Trading Cards! Yep! It's our gift to you guys for being so awesome, and something cool for the new players!

Here's a sneak preview

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/f73547582f5242952eb67a308997a4384fc1d17b.jpg[/img]

Speaking of new players, if you have Speed Limit on your Wishlist and have been on the fence about buying it, [b]Speed Limit is now 60% OFF[/b]!

notes.title: Speed Limit - A Roller Coaster Year
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/bfe3f244bfd6d472950abd550fe48b3cdf3794dd.jpg[/img]

It feels like Speed Limit had launched only yesterday. We shipped polished builds to game stores a month prior, sent review keys to press and streamers, and were eagerly anticipating for players to finally play the game.

We imagined Speed Limit as joyful and mischievous ode to the golden era of arcade games, so we were relieved when the first, mostly very positive impressions started to come in via reviews, streams, tweets, etc.

[h2]Here are some of your thoughts that made us all warm and fuzzy or made us laugh. <3[/h2]

[i]"Retro platform shooter + fast + rides = Remember that movie Die Hard? Well, this is Die Damn Easy. Thankfully there are infinite lives and you respawn at checkpoints. Feels like some Matrix scenes."[/i]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/exodust00/recommended/1058280]Exodust[/url]

[i]"You can tell this game was made with care, and the developers really appreciated the games of the era that the game pays homage to."[/i]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/MrUnbecoming/recommended/1058280]MrUnbecoming[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/c90b8bb64c616c490d50890f96463bdc56704cae.jpg[/img]

[i]"I recommend this game if you're a masochist and don't mind dying hundreds of times."[/i]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/mamefan/recommended/1058280]MAME-FAN[/url]

[h2]Press also made some nice comments. :)[/h2]

[i]"In all my years of gaming I don’t think I have ever played a more fast-paced game than Speed Limit."[/i]
[url=https://www.gamegrin.com/reviews/speed-limit-review/]Alana Dunitz, GameGrin[/url]

[i]"It’s like all the Fast & Furious movies crammed into one, over the top pixel package that just keeps getting more and more outlandish by the level. In fact, Speed Limit is better than Fast & Furious, because nobody ever talks about the importance of family."[/i]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJS6iW1SFyc]Defunct Games[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/950e20da827e7f3edce7c2f8509c2d7e55f52d7a.png[/img]

[i]"Speed Limit is a work of art that makes you question the sanity of the developers."[/i]
[url=https://stoffelpresents.com/speed-limit-ps4-review]Badger Nimahson, Stoffel Presents[/url]

[i]"The game is just snowballing craziness from beginning to end, and that should come as no surprise when you look at the Croatian developer’s official website and notice that all of the developers on the Speed Limit page use groundhog pictures to represent team members instead of portraits. That’s bizarre and I’m here for it."[/i]
[b]Jake Arias, Killa Penguin[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/f626fa027a7ee3dfe52ff1ef74e7a5bbe2702b2e.png[/img]
[i]It's true, though[/i]

[h2]Arcade Edition and Penny & Dime Edition[/h2]

We also listened to your complaints and thoughts on how to make the game better. We felt that adding new [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1058280/view/4755214150655562800]Arcade, Neon[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1058280/view/2975177715972387720]Kiosk modes[/url] would enhance and prolong the experience, while keeping the spirit of the game intact.

[previewyoutube=7_OL0borVkM;full][/previewyoutube]

The Arcade mode was also added to the demo, so feel free to check it out. If you already have the game, what are you waiting for? [b]All updates are free.[/b] Cheers! :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/bcd9bbd4cdc0f781f9037dc654d89c3f2018ba46.jpg[/img]
[i]Free as in free beer, but don't drink and drive[/i]

We also invite you to share your best scores on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/stats/1058280/leaderboards/6473700/]Steam leaderboards[/url], or a [url=https://www.speedrun.com/speed_limit]Speedrun database[/url], or just brag on [url=https://game-chuck.com/discord]our Discord channel[/url].

[h2]Nominations and Laurels[/h2]

Speaking of bragging, we want to share some of the accolades and recognition we received following the launch. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/2999eb12860f4d95dd866316bed3b8c1b5472f53.png[/img]

Thank you for reading! :) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/5a3c995a6c95cab12658de428b279704d4d8106d.gif[/img]

We hope you have wonderful holidays and the bestest of best 2022!

notes.title: Speed Limit: Penny & Dime Edition at gamescom
notes.content:
We released a new (second) update for Speed Limit at gamescom called the "[b]Penny & Dime Edition[/b]!" 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/29d16f91d41a54ded5f6e4f60262bf941fa8bf2c.png[/img]

Penny & Dime Edition is a content update that features a new game mode called the “[b]Kiosk Mode[/b],” a faithful recreation of the arcade cabinet user experience that enables integration with coin-operated arcade cabinets. 

[h2]Kiosk Mode[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/c703a968c1f0a6a3affa539265bd9326c4f95bfb.png[/img]

Kiosk Mode was designed for our very own line of arcade cabinets titled the "[b][url=https://game-chuck.com/gamechuck-arcades/]Gamechuck Arcades[/url][/b]" and upon completion, we thought that the hardcore arcade community might also appreciate its addition to the commercial game version. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/02dcc26a73233d9ed965b01e7d60e129dc86db28.png[/img]

Kiosk Mode replicates the challenges set in the previously released Arcade Mode, but with the exception that you can now [b]customize the credits and lives system[/b] in the special menu, as well as [b]modify graphics and audio settings[/b], as if you were a real arcade operator. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/5f337032cb48483fdc691a6e2e3f6c7a8c3c0d35.png[/img]

We like to think that it adds another level of immersion to the true arcade experience we always envisioned, especially if you own an arcade cabinet.

[h2]Penny & Dime Edition trailer[/h2]

Here’s the new Speed Limit Penny & Dime Edition trailer that showcases both the current and previous update titled the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1058280/view/4755214150655562800]"Arcade Edition"[/url] in action:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_OL0borVkM

Speed Limit will also be [b]50% off on sale[/b] during gamescom, from 25 to 27 August.

We hope you enjoy the new update and the game! :)

notes.title: Welcome to Speed Limit: Arcade Edition!
notes.content:
Following the Speed Limit launch, we are now a bit smarter in terms of what you liked, and what you wanted to have improved in the game.

In our minds, the game longevity, the number of levels, the difficulty is perfectly balanced, as all things should be, but seeing what you guys wrote in your reviews, in the comments on the Discussion Boards, and our Discord server, we've decided to make your wishes true.

In the first [b]MAJOR [/b]update for Speed Limit, we are bringing [b]TWO brand-new game modes[/b].

[h2]Arcade Mode[/h2]

Just like the classics of the 80s, Arcade Mode delivers a classic arcade experience with a CRT-like visual overlay and a standard credits and lives system. 

[url=https://imgur.com/G3fQ9JW][img]https://i.imgur.com/G3fQ9JW.gif[/img][/url]

You get to choose how many coins to insert before starting the game, including the option for unlimited credits, allowing players to tailor the difficulty to their own tastes.

[url=https://imgur.com/oZQGbWg][img]http://i.imgur.com/oZQGbWg.gif[/img][/url]

Of course, as with the golden age of the arcade, part of the fun was chasing that high score and comparing it with your friends. As such, Arcade Mode also replicates this by featuring a high-score counter to compete and compare your results with friends, contributing to much higher replayability.

[url=https://imgur.com/E3OzFMW][img]http://i.imgur.com/E3OzFMW.gif[/img][/url]

[h2]Neon Mode[/h2]

For players who are more in the mood for a little bit of relaxation, Neon Mode has them covered. 

[url=https://imgur.com/DPO7lxq][img]http://i.imgur.com/DPO7lxq.gif[/img][/url]

In Neon Mode players once again jump on the bike before cruising along the highway in a neon-glowing recreation of the original game’s motorcycle levels, inspired by the synthwave track Neon Limit.

[url=https://imgur.com/RyiE1ti][img]http://i.imgur.com/RyiE1ti.gif[/img][/url]

Additionally, the Neon Limit track is also available for casual listening in a freshly added in-game music player.

notes.title: Backstage insight into Speed Limit development
notes.content:
Speed Limit is gearing towards its release on Steam and consoles quite soon, and we surely wouldn't want to keep you in dark on how the development of the game currently goes.

In short - the development is going great, and all we have to do is to make some smaller changes, bug fixes, and there is a console port, too, which is done by our publisher Chorus Worldwide.

So, to keep you a bit occupied while you wait for Speed Limit, we made this "news digest" of sorts that contains our blog posts that we made to date. Let's get to it, then!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/d2154615f53bd3727338b277826b88f452338b1b.jpg[/img]

[h2]How we made pixel art for Speed Limit[/h2]

For this blog, we have invited our experienced pixel artist, Jurica who will answer some of our (silly) questions – just for your convenience.

Additionally, Jurica made five timelapse videos showing how he does pixel art (using Aseprite), which can help you with your pixel art endeavors.

[b]What drove you into pixel art?[/b]

Easier learning curve and probably a bit of nostalgia. I got my first computer, Commodore 64 when I was 3.

[b]Can you describe the process of making a pixel art character for Speed Limit?[/b]

[olist]
[*] Our game designer and project lead describe the feature, and an effect they want to achieve with the piece required.
[*] Google all the stuff we talked about because I don’t know half of the words used. Also to draw inspiration from different existing technologies/equipment and make some kind of composition.
[*] I draw 2-3 variations following the game art style as much as I can, and then we iterate on the best variation.
[*] Profit
[/olist]

[b]How do you make animations for Speed Limit?[/b]

It depends on what I’m working on.

If it’s character animation, I start with just a gesture line or a silhouette of the motion that we want to achieve. Then I grind out the details following the basic design in a few iterations until everyone is happy with the smoothness and motion of the animation.

[b]How difficult is it to make pixel art?[/b]

It is easy to start and difficult to master. You can get away with a lot of stuff, but also exaggerate other. You need to learn color theory, anatomy, composition, general 2d art, basics of animation, you name it. I still feel I have much more to learn than I know and have my work cut out for me for some time.

[b]If I wanted to start making some pixel art, where should I start?[/b]

Easiest and fastest – I would recommend an online app https://www.piskelapp.com/ that is easy to use and has basic animation covered.

Then open up a YouTube pixel art tutorial or a Twitter tutorial, e.g. Pedro Medeiros and just go wild, and most importantly, be consistent.

Read [url=https://game-chuck.com/2020/05/04/how-to-start-with-pixel-art-if-youre-a-noob/]the rest of the blog[/url].

[h2]How we made our own soundtrack for Speed Limit?[/h2]

One of the primary reasons why DOOM from 2016 was so damn awesome is Mick Gordon's incredible soundtrack.

And one of the reasons why Speed Limit will be awesome is our sound designer and soundtrack composer - Matija. F YEAH!!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/b208bc67d47dee55c9d9a8fdab89cfc39818b089.jpg[/img]

I used to work as a school teacher, but following a collaboration with Gamechuck that lasted a few years, I got a full-time job here.

I started working on Speed Limit music when I first saw sketches of levels.

Since the start, we were thinking of a [url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CHajdWVsHVh/]synthwave soundtrack[/url]. 

Ten tracks in, after playing a prototype level I have noticed that there will be a problem: The game was too fast and synthwave wasn’t giving that much of a kick and adrenaline to the player.

I was thinking; “I don’t want to make another metal soundtrack. It is the easy way out and it doesn’t reflect the atmosphere of the game at all.”

[url=https://soundcloud.com/malatestinic/sets/speed-limit-ost][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/1e61d059aa228e4bba70a90882a85897981dc7ee.jpg[/img][/url]

So I went to explore my possibilities. I did it the fun way: played playlists of music while playing the level.

After a week or two of testing and making music, I have noticed that music from the bands like The Prodigy, Noisia, Pendulum, etc. clicked immediately.

[previewyoutube=XQEBzauVIlA;full][/previewyoutube]

Matija goes really in detail on how we made the soundtrack, so make sure to [url=https://game-chuck.com/2020/11/17/this-is-how-we-made-our-awesome-speed-limit-soundtrack/]read his full blog[/url]!

[h2]How we made those incredible transitions in Speed Limit?[/h2]

And now, the star of the show - Speed Limit transitions. Speed Limit is a genre-changing rollercoaster. The game seamlessly changes perspectives AND gameplay - as you play. Our programmer Karlo is gonna share a bit of his magic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/69546ae3661da17d2ecaaeac5c20f34fd555525b.jpg[/img]

Some transitions were hard to explain by words so we made some animations just to be able to visualize them clearly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/f3908440d10e34eeee700a99a2cbcf6262656563.gif[/img]

Once I had that picture in my mind, I started making some preparations for both levels which was mostly positioning objects where they should be at the start or end of a transition, and discussing with lead developer Vanja to do the same for the other two levels that happen before and after mine.

In the meantime, our pixel artist Jurica chucked out all the necessary assets with their changing perspectives (ex. choppa rotating from a sidescrolling perspective to isometric perspective).

Finally it was transition time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/e0d26c66d83054c2522df49860ba88771b126e90.gif[/img]

The majority of each transition consists of interpolating objects between key positions and scales, playing their animations at the right speed and time, and warping the background in several ways. Most of the work here was properly sequencing all the events and tweaking them to look and feel good.

Few issues arose during the making which required making some creative solutions. One example is the background during bike-to-choppa transition.

In the bike level, the road and sea background is constructed from segments, and you can see tall buildings. In the choppa level, the background is a simple warped scrolling texture of water.

How do you transition between these two? The answer is that you don’t. When the player hits the choppa after jumping on a ramp, the camera zooms into the choppa, covering up the entire screen. That’s when we remove some elements from the background (like the road and buildings) to make the transition easier.

The car-to-bike transition had a slightly different story. We had to draw a tunnel that transitions from a top-down perspective to a fake 3D perspective, ending with a camera behind the player inside that tunnel. How?

For this one, I went overboard and actually reconstructed the whole transition in 3D using the Godot engine. Then I recorded the positions of vertices of the tunnel, projected onto the camera’s 2D plane during the animation.

Finally, I added these positions into the level, and now I had exact coordinates of tunnel vertices. All that was left was to draw the segments between them. So in essence, the tunnel you see during the transition, it’s drawn with baked coordinates from a 3D animation. Whew! It paid off in the end.

[url=https://game-chuck.com/2020/11/30/this-is-how-we-made-awesome-transitions-in-speed-limit/]Read the whole blog[/url]!

[h2]How we use illusions for perspective changes in Speed Limit[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/4af9a62ff5ea7e509a568521703454c0fdb17640.jpg[/img]

We are ending this Speed Limit news digest with a real gem: a [url=https://game-chuck.com/2020/12/09/how-we-use-illusions-for-perspective-changes-in-speed-limit/]blog post[/url] by our lead programmer, Vanja who explains how we use illusions for those perspective changes in Speed Limit.

If you were to take the game camera in any game anywhere you would like to. You would soon discover that the game worlds are illusions because the content outside of the player’s view ends with empty voids. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/66b1ea6943d5df84a5ac723bbfc17b279a53c541.gif[/img]

Speed Limit is no exception to this and so our transitions are illusions where we hide things out of the player’s view or simply obscure certain elements during transitions to bring the player’s attention to a specific part of the screen.

Changing perspectives in Speed Limit was one of the big challenges because everything we render on screen only uses the X and Y axis, the third Z axis is always 0 and the camera projection matrix is set up for 2D orthographic projection.

While it is possible to go full 3D with GameMaker Studio 2, going 3D for transitions would not help making them happen.

The transition for the outro to the train section was made out of a very special train carriage. The carriage has 4 images that we stretch in order to fake perspective changes. The road is made out of 2 images (fence, and the road itself) while the train tracks are just stretched out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/600f03587ab084495e9aa8e4be73193c5a670385.gif[/img]

The background city is just moved above and outside the screen so the water ends up covering the top of the screen. Once this change is made, a tunnel entrance always sitting outside of the camera view to the right is brought into view and it covers the train and brings the repeated tile pattern from the car section in.

After the pattern covers the entire screen we immediately swap to the car section as seamlessly as possible. The car itself has an animation where the perspective changes which Jurica animated by hand.

[url=https://game-chuck.com/2020/12/09/how-we-use-illusions-for-perspective-changes-in-speed-limit/]Read the rest of the blog[/url]!

notes.title: What is Speed Limit and why should you care?
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=NiNMaHEsI3c;full][/previewyoutube]

Speed Limit is a genre-changing, perspective-changing retro pixel-art rollercoaster. Now that's a mouthful, huh?

What if we told you that all that genre-changing and perspective-changing is done seamlessly - while you play the game. Yep. 

Or, as one of the comments from YouTube summed it up:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/0a1f55f50f4d5a25bf425546ab10bffcab63b661.jpg[/img]

Here's how it looks in-game (minus the heavy GIF image quality compression):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/0fbcd00e390ece0a175664fc205b8654d8f59303.gif[/img]


The idea came from our genius creative director, Igor Kolar who is a fan of all things retro, and all things 90s, so he wanted to put it together in a super-fast and super-difficult video game we call Speed Limit.

The main inspiration for the game was the 90s movies, mainly with Bruce Willis and his Die Hard movies.

Hence the meme

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/b47a2b80855e56f4b9e3709d4dcc27f182ad4f31.jpg[/img]

At Gamechuck we are also massive, massive fans of retro consoles, retro games, and that sweet retro look. That's why we thought pixel-art would be the best fit for Speed Limit.

Obviously, we didn't want to make "yet another pixel-art platformer". Speed Limit is a fun, addictive, good-looking, and pretty difficult game. In this game, you will die a lot. But, worry not. We've heard our game testers and introduced checkpoints, and easy mode.

Btw, wanna try the game? You can play the demo [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1058280/Speed_Limit/]RIGHT NOW![/url]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1058280/Speed_Limit/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/d6e79f3e9ec269842cf05ee6bf0c2a34411fb7d8.png[/img][/url]

Let us know how you liked it in the comments!

GG!

notes.title: BIG updates in Speed Limit demo!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826372/3fbb823dc87c0dc3caa6d2b48e4e6d9cd174bee1.jpg[/img]

Well hello there, dear Gamechuckers! We hope you're doing great and keeping yourselves safe.

We have some great news for you. We've been working really hard on Speed Limit for the past several weeks and made some fantastic progress in the game. And yes, we have been [b]closely listening to your feedback[/b]. 

In order to show you what we've done, we have updated the free demo on Steam with some great stuff you can expect in the final game.

So, what's new?

[list]
[*] [b]a cool new menu screen:[/b] We have completely revamped the menu screen which is now more clear and features a piece of new background music made by our music and sound designer, Matija.
[*] [b]updated control scheme:[/b] The third level now supports a twin-stick control scheme.
[*] [b]better learning curve:[/b] We have introduced checkpoints for levels 1 and 2 so you can learn the levels better, and perhaps try-out different tactics?
[*] [b]levels 1, 2, and 3 revamped and longer:[/b] All the levels have been revamped, and made longer, while the third level has been re-designed from the ground-up.
[*] [b]many more bug fixes and feedback implementations:[/b] Well, this is self-explanatory!
[/list]

Try it, play it, and let us know how you like it!
